correctness.rationale: The successive ratio is θhⱼ and its forward difference changes sign at the strictly decreasing γⱼ, so for 2<r<7 the ratios above one form a finite integer interval and H is attained at m(r), including the tie case. Two modal blocks require that interval to be nonempty and the first step to be strictly down. At θ=1/H there is no upward step; at θh₁=1 in the middle regime the initial flat block is followed by a rise, so it is not a mode. For r≤2 all ratios are below one, and for r≥7 they are nonincreasing. For the global threshold the individual crossing levels bₖ tend to 1 and all exceed 1/H. The proof also supplies some bₖ strictly below the upper chamber edge: p₃>p₁ at the formal first-ratio equality for 3<r<7 and pₖ/p₁ grows as k^(r−2) at formal θ=1 for 2<r≤3. Together these facts give finite attainment and strict location; the comparison with each bₖ then proves all global cases. Near r=2, the continuous maximizer and rounding error give the quadratic width, and the two simple roots of cz²−z+1 give the divergent extremum indices. At γ₂=17/5 an index-two tie is allowed and H=2(r+2)/9 throughout the stated upper regime, giving the exact width. The two witnesses at r=6 check directly. Independently counted exact plateau components at strict and boundary parameters, including a two-count second peak and r=7 with a three-count single modal block.
residual_risks: The finite probes illustrate the boundary conventions; the ratio topology and analytic tail argument supply the infinite-support claims.
